summary: A Comair Canadair Regional Jet CRJ-100 operating as Delta Connection Flight 5191 crashed on takeoff from Lexington's Blue Grass Airport to Atlanta at 6:07 a.m. ET yesterday, killing 49 people on board and seriously injuring first officer James M. Polehinke; Polehinke was taken to the University of Kentucky's Chandler Medical Center in critical condition and the aircraft tail number was confirmed as N431CA. The National Transportation Safety Board, based on flight data recorder information and scene evidence, is focusing on the theory that the pilot attempted to take off from a 3,500-foot runway not certified for airline traffic instead of the cleared 7,000-foot runway and investigators believe the plane did not reach sufficient speed to lift off; Fayette County coroner Gary Ginn said there was a significant post-impact fire, the aircraft moved several hundred yards, remained largely intact with most passengers still in the cabin, and he expects fire to be the cause of death for the majority of victims. Local police, firefighters and two off-duty officers responded quickly and helped pull Polehinke from the cockpit; the FAA told CNN there is no indication of terrorism, families have been taken to a local hotel with Comair staff assisting and a hotline (1-800-801-0088) has been set up, and among the dead were newlyweds Jon Hooker and Scarlett Parsley and other passengers including Charles Lykins, Mike Finley and flight attendant Kelly Heyer.
